name: zeek_run
description: Run the installed Zeek over a capture and read its logs back as records, with what ran recorded: the Zeek version as printed, the command, whether checksums were validated (-C is passed unless checksum_validation is true), and a policy script the tool writes into out_dir (by default one that loads policy/frameworks/files/hash-all-files; `policies` changes the list, an empty list loads nothing; a policy is a name Zeek resolves, never a path or a script from the evidence) with its path and SHA-256. Whether the installed build has a policy by that name, and which hash functions it computes, is not assumed: hashes_produced says whether any files.log record carries a hash value (hash_fields only names the columns, which a real install can have whether or not they were filled). The reader follows each log's own header (#separator, #set_separator, #empty_field, #unset_field, #fields, #types), \xNN escapes, sets and vectors as lists, typed numbers, and every time as raw text with a decoded `_utc` beside it; JSON logs are read too. A record that does not fit (a wrong column count, a value that is not its type, bad JSON, no header) is counted with its line and byte offset and kept whole in malformed-<log>.jsonl, and ok is false. Requested logs Zeek did not write are listed apart from logs written with no records; reporter, weird and capture_loss are always summarised (capture_loss exists only if its policy is loaded, so its absence is not a finding). conn.log rows are Zeek connections as Zeek defines them, not application data delivered. Every log stays whole in out_dir, named, and inline records are bounded by limit. SENSITIVE: logs can carry credentials, cookies and request URIs. The directory is private (0700/0600); inline records withhold secret-named fields and the hash of an object under 128 bytes, redact URLs, and scrub every other string except identifiers, hashes, fingerprints, addresses and times (by shape: a short secret in free text is not recognised); run it as a job with secret_output: true. Zeek runs in the tool's own process group (the harness ending the tool ends Zeek; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP kill it), and timeout_seconds is held under the manifest's limit. A failing `zeek --version` makes the run not ok.

out_dir.description: An empty directory under work/ (in a job, under $OUT; work/<your agent id>/name is mapped to $OUT/name) where Zeek runs and its logs land. It is private (0700, files 0600)

logs.description: Which logs to return inline, e.g. ["conn","dns","ssl"] (default: every log written). A name Zeek did not write is listed in logs_requested_not_written; reporter, weird and capture_loss are summarised regardless

limit.description: Maximum records per log returned inline (default 200); the whole log is the file named in its entry, and omitted says how many were not returned

timeout_seconds.description: Kill Zeek, and everything it started, after this long (10 to 1100 seconds, default 900), so that this tool stops Zeek before the 1200-second limit does

policies.description: Zeek policy names to load through the script the tool writes (default ["policy/frameworks/files/hash-all-files"]; [] loads none). Names only: a path, a name that climbs out of Zeek's script path or one under inputs/ is refused

checksum_validation.description: Leave Zeek's checksum validation on (default false: -C is passed, and the answer says checksums were not validated)
